fixes.explanation: That's the one, baker. David prays, "Answer me when I call, O God of my righteousness! You have relieved my distress…" (Psalm 4:1). He asks God to answer, and he also remembers that God relieved his distress. I think remembering what God has done is a smart way to pray.
Right, it's False. David asks, "How long will you love vanity and seek after lies?" (Psalm 4:2). The verse names vanity and lies, not truth. So the statement doesn't match what the text says.
That's the line: "Be angry, yet do not sin…" (Psalm 4:4). It doesn't say anger is the problem. The command is about what you do with it. Honestly, friend, that's a tall order.
Right. The verse says, "Offer the sacrifices of the righteous and trust in the LORD." (Psalm 4:5). The two commands sit side by side. Trusting in the LORD is the second one.

Seven days, friend? With no cookies, I'd be a crumb by day two. The verse says, "Offer the sacrifices of the righteous and trust in the LORD." (Psalm 4:5). Fasting isn't mentioned there. The second command is to trust in the LORD.

Good thought, baker, but Jerusalem isn't mentioned in this psalm. The verse says, "Offer the sacrifices of the righteous and trust in the LORD." (Psalm 4:5). The second command is to trust in the LORD.
That's right. Many ask, "Who can show us the good?" and David says, "Shine the light of Your face upon us, O LORD." (Psalm 4:6). His prayer goes to the LORD.

I see why you'd go there, baker, but the psalm doesn't mention priests. After many ask their question, David says, "Shine the light of Your face upon us, O LORD." (Psalm 4:6). He prays to the LORD Himself.

Yep, and look at the size of that. David says, "You have filled my heart with more joy than when grain and new wine abound." (Psalm 4:7). He compares his joy to a time when grain and new wine abound, and says God gave him more. I can't even picture it, and I've seen a full cookie rack.

It's actually True, baker. The verse says, "You have filled my heart with more joy than when grain and new wine abound." (Psalm 4:7). The word is "more." God filled his heart with more joy than when grain and new wine abound.

That's the reason, baker. David says, "I will lie down and sleep in peace, for You alone, O LORD, make me dwell in safety." (Psalm 4:8). The word "alone" points to the LORD as the One who makes him dwell in safety.
